dataset.question: What are the ethical obligations of annotators in evaluation pipelines, and how are they addressed in the document?
dataset.reference_answer: The ethical obligations of annotators in evaluation pipelines include privacy, consent and notice, access control, and third-party exposure. Annotators are exposed to toxic, violent, or disturbing content by design, and must be informed about content nature before assignment. Obligations include rotation limits, mandatory breaks for heavy-content queues, opt-out without penalty, access to support resources, and compensation that reflects the burden. Exposure hours per rater are tracked as an operational limit, not an afterthought. For general annotation, fair pay and reasonable throughput targets are quality issues too — exploited raters produce drifted labels (Chapter 77).

dataset.question: What are the three measurement layers used in RAG evaluation and how are they defined?
dataset.reference_answer: The three measurement layers in RAG evaluation are retrieval quality, generation quality, and end-to-end quality. Retrieval quality assesses whether the right documents appear in the context window, measured with ranking metrics such as recall@k and nDCG. Generation quality asks whether the answer is faithful to the retrieved evidence, relevant to the question, and complete. End-to-end quality asks whether the user's actual task succeeds, which may tolerate imperfect intermediate steps.

dataset.question: What is the empirical fact used in stability testing that distinguishes grounded answers from fabrications, and how does it relate to the reliability of a system in generating answers?
dataset.reference_answer: The empirical fact used in stability testing is that grounded answers are reproducible, while fabrications are not. Sampling the same question multiple times and measuring agreement gives a reference-free signal of reliability — and a probe for system fragility. This fact is central to the evaluation of answer stability in RAG systems.

faithfulness.label: Faithfulness
faithfulness.description: Fraction of answer claims supported by the exact evidence supplied to the generator.

answer_relevancy.label: Answer relevancy
answer_relevancy.description: Cosine similarity of the question to questions reconstructed from the answer, penalizing noncommittal answers. Negative cosine values are possible.

context_precision.label: Context precision
context_precision.description: Rank-sensitive precision of retrieved text judged against the source reference answer.

context_recall.label: Context recall
context_recall.description: Fraction of reference answer claims supported by the retrieved text.

factual_correctness.label: Factual correctness
factual_correctness.description: Claim-level F1 of the generated answer against the source reference answer.

multimodal_faithfulness.label: Visual faithfulness
multimodal_faithfulness.description: Answer grounding in the actual text and image evidence; requires a judge with vision support.

precision_at_k.label: Precision@k
precision_at_k.description: Relevant unique retrieved chunks divided by the declared retrieval cutoff k. Missing slots count against precision.

recall_at_k.label: Recall@k
recall_at_k.description: Fraction of source-labelled relevant evidence retrieved. With equivalent supporting-passage groups, one matching chunk covers each group; otherwise the denominator is the positive labelled chunk count.

mrr.label: MRR
mrr.description: Reciprocal rank of the first relevant chunk, or zero if none is retrieved.

ndcg_at_k.label: nDCG@k
ndcg_at_k.description: Discounted graded relevance of the retrieved ranking relative to the ideal source-labelled ranking.

hit_rate_at_k.label: Hit rate@k
hit_rate_at_k.description: One when at least one relevant chunk appears in the first k unique results, otherwise zero.

map_at_k.label: MAP@k
map_at_k.description: Per-question average precision at relevant ranks divided by min(k, number of relevant chunks); the report averages these values.

normalized_exact_match.label: Exact match
normalized_exact_match.description: Exact reference match after Unicode, case and whitespace normalization. This lexical diagnostic does not establish correctness.

token_f1.label: Token F1
token_f1.description: Lexical token overlap F1 against the reference; preserves numeric differences and does not measure semantic correctness.

citation_page_validity.label: Citation page validity
citation_page_validity.description: Fraction of cited page numbers present in the actual retrieved evidence. Structural validity does not establish claim support.

citation_page_coverage.label: Citation evidence-page coverage
citation_page_coverage.description: Fraction of labelled reference pages mentioned in citations. Equivalent page alternatives count once when supplied. This is evidence-page coverage, not answer-claim coverage.
citation_page_coverage.applicability: answerable cases with source page labels

citation_source_validity.label: Citation source validity
citation_source_validity.description: Fraction of cited source numbers corresponding to actual generator sources. Structural validity does not establish semantic support.

abstention_accuracy.label: Correct abstention
abstention_accuracy.description: Judge classification of whether an unanswerable response explicitly abstains without inventing an answer.

false_answer_rate.label: False-answer rate
false_answer_rate.description: One minus correct abstention, on explicitly labelled unanswerable cases only.

failure_rate.label: Failed or partial attempt rate
failure_rate.description: Failed or partial samples divided by completed, partial and failed attempts; cancelled samples are excluded.

error_rate.label: Error rate
error_rate.description: Failed samples divided by completed, partial and failed attempts; cancelled samples are excluded.

partial_rate.label: Partial-result rate
partial_rate.description: Partial samples divided by completed, partial and failed attempts; cancelled samples are excluded.

retrieval_seconds.label: Retrieval seconds
retrieval_seconds.description: Measured duration, including completed and failed attempts with recorded timing; cache replay remains included. p50/p95 use linear interpolation over observed values.

local_retrieval_seconds.description: Measured duration, including completed and failed attempts with recorded timing; cache replay remains included. p50/p95 use linear interpolation over observed values.
